ascendancy.mental_hook: Not rising. Having risen, and on top.
ascendancy.semantic_hint: The dominant position one faction holds over another.

incorrect_associations.misconception: loses the certainty that defines it

ascertain.required_nuance: establishing something as certain, not merely learning it
ascertain.mental_hook: Not just find out. Find out for sure.
ascertain.semantic_hint: What an inspector does to the facts before signing the report.

incorrect_associations.misconception: hears 'aesthetic', which is nearly the opposite

ascetic.required_nuance: self-denial chosen, usually for spiritual reasons
ascetic.mental_hook: One letter from aesthetic, and its opposite in practice.
ascetic.semantic_hint: How a monk lives who sleeps on a board and eats once a day.

ascribe.required_nuance: assigning a cause or an author
ascribe.semantic_hint: What you do when you put a success down to hard work.

incorrect_associations.misconception: misses the negating 'a-' and lands on the opposite

aseptic.required_nuance: no germs present, the 'a-' negating septic
aseptic.mental_hook: The 'a' turns septic into its opposite.
aseptic.semantic_hint: What an operating theatre has to be kept.

askance.required_nuance: a sideways look that means doubt
askance.semantic_hint: How you look at someone when you do not believe a word of it.

accepted_concepts: a rough edge in the voice
asperity.required_nuance: harshness in tone or manner, not in content
asperity.mental_hook: The roughness in the voice, not what it says.
asperity.semantic_hint: The sharp edge in someone's voice when their patience has gone.

aspersion.required_nuance: a remark that damages a reputation
aspersion.semantic_hint: The damaging remark someone casts at another's good name.

aspersions.required_nuance: remarks damaging a reputation, cast rather than stated
aspersions.mental_hook: The set phrase is to "cast" them.
aspersions.semantic_hint: What someone casts when they slur another's good name.

assail.required_nuance: attack, physical or verbal, and forceful
assail.mental_hook: Fists or words. Either way, an attack.
assail.semantic_hint: What critics do to a policy they hate, and what soldiers do to a wall.

incorrect_associations.misconception: takes the weaker sense and loses the testing

assay.required_nuance: testing to determine quality or content
assay.mental_hook: What the mint does to a sample of gold.
assay.semantic_hint: What a laboratory does to a gold sample to find its purity.

assent.mental_hook: Two letters from ascent, and no climbing involved.
assent.semantic_hint: The formal agreement a monarch gives to a new law.

assert.required_nuance: stated with confidence, not necessarily proven
assert.mental_hook: Said with confidence. Not the same as shown to be true.
assert.semantic_hint: What you do when you state something firmly without proving it.

assertive.mental_hook: Between passive and aggressive, which is the whole point of the word.
assertive.semantic_hint: The word for standing up for yourself without being hostile about it.

assiduous.required_nuance: care sustained over a long stretch
assiduous.mental_hook: Sits at it until it is done properly.
assiduous.semantic_hint: The word for a researcher who checks every source twice.

assiduously.required_nuance: care kept up over a long stretch
assiduously.mental_hook: Steadily, and for as long as it takes.
assiduously.semantic_hint: How someone works who checks every detail, every time.

assimilate.mental_hook: Taken in until you cannot tell it was ever separate.
assimilate.semantic_hint: What a body does to food, and a culture does to newcomers.

accepted_concepts: calm a grief or a hunger
assuage.required_nuance: easing a feeling or an appetite
assuage.mental_hook: Grief, guilt, hunger, thirst. Feelings, mostly.
assuage.semantic_hint: What an apology does to someone's anger.

astonishment.required_nuance: surprise strong enough to stop you
astonishment.semantic_hint: What you feel when something happens that you thought impossible.

incorrect_associations.misconception: hears 'stringent' and swaps severity of tone for severity of rule

astringent.mental_hook: Makes your mouth pucker, or your critics wince.
astringent.semantic_hint: What witch hazel does to skin, and what a harsh review does to an author.

astute.required_nuance: shrewdness, often about seizing an advantage
astute.semantic_hint: The word for an investor who spots the opportunity everyone else misses.

asunder.semantic_hint: How something is torn when it is ripped clean in two.

accepted_concepts: the return of an ancestral trait
a throwback to an earlier form
the resurfacing of a primitive characteristic
a reappearance out of the past

incorrect_associations.misconception: inverts a return into a novelty

atavism.required_nuance: something old resurfacing, never something new
atavism.mental_hook: The ancestor, showing up again generations later.
atavism.semantic_hint: When a trait skips generations and suddenly reappears.

attenuate.mental_hook: Signals, arguments and risks are all thinned this way.
attenuate.semantic_hint: What distance does to a radio signal.

incorrect_associations.misconception: confuses a settled stance with one passing view

attitude.required_nuance: settled and habitual, not a passing opinion
attitude.mental_hook: Not what you think today. How you tend to think.
attitude.semantic_hint: The settled outlook someone brings to everything they meet.

incorrect_associations.misconception: takes the verb sense for the noun

attribute.required_nuance: a quality belonging to a thing
attribute.mental_hook: What the thing has, not what you say about it.
attribute.semantic_hint: One of the qualities that together make a thing what it is.

incorrect_associations.answer: tuned in the musical sense only

attuned.required_nuance: adjusted so as to be receptive
attuned.mental_hook: Tuned, but to a mood rather than a note.
attuned.semantic_hint: What a good manager is to the mood of the room.

accepted_concepts: willing to risk a great deal
audacious.semantic_hint: The word for a plan so bold it makes people gasp.

audacity.mental_hook: Admired in a plan. Resented in a person.
audacity.semantic_hint: What someone has when they ask for a raise on their first day.

accepted_concepts: add to in order to strengthen
augment.semantic_hint: What a second income does to a salary.

accepted_concepts: a sign of what is to come
augury.mental_hook: The Romans read birds for these.
augury.semantic_hint: The sign a Roman priest read in the flight of birds.

incorrect_associations.misconception: takes the proper noun for the adjective

august.mental_hook: Not the month. The quality the month was named for.
august.semantic_hint: The adjective for an institution so venerable you lower your voice in it.

incorrect_associations.misconception: confuses the sponsorship with the omens the word came from

auspices.required_nuance: backing and protection, almost always "under the"
auspices.semantic_hint: The sponsorship a conference is held under.

accepted_concepts: a promising sign for what follows

incorrect_associations.misconception: inverts the good omen into a bad one

auspicious.mental_hook: A good sign for what comes next.
auspicious.semantic_hint: The adjective for a start that bodes well for everything after.

austere.mental_hook: A room with one chair and no pictures.
austere.semantic_hint: What a room is with bare walls, one chair and nothing else.

authoritarian.mental_hook: Authoritative is trusted. This one is obeyed.
authoritarian.semantic_hint: The word for a regime that permits no disagreement at all.

incorrect_associations.misconception: inverts rule by one into rule by many

autocratic.required_nuance: power concentrated in one person, unchecked
autocratic.mental_hook: One person decides. Everyone else complies.
autocratic.semantic_hint: The word for a ruler whose power nobody can check.

accepted_concepts: make a process run by machine
have a machine do it instead

incorrect_associations.misconception: confuses being self-operating with making something so

automate.required_nuance: converting manual work into machine work
automate.mental_hook: The job still gets done. Nobody does it.
automate.semantic_hint: What a factory does to a job that used to need hands.

incorrect_associations.misconception: hears 'automatic' and swaps independence for mechanism

autonomous.required_nuance: governs itself, answering to no one
autonomous.mental_hook: Decides for itself, rather than merely running by itself.
autonomous.semantic_hint: The word for a region that governs itself within a larger state.

autonomy.mental_hook: One letter from anatomy, and about freedom rather than bodies.
autonomy.semantic_hint: What a region wins when it gains the right to govern itself.

incorrect_associations.misconception: guesses from a vaguely similar sound

auxiliary.required_nuance: supporting and additional, never the main thing
auxiliary.mental_hook: The backup generator, not the grid.
auxiliary.semantic_hint: What the backup generator is to the main power supply.

avarice.semantic_hint: The deadly sin of wanting more money without limit.

avaricious.mental_hook: Not merely wanting. Never having enough.
avaricious.semantic_hint: The adjective for a landlord who raises the rent every chance he gets.

aver.mental_hook: One letter from avert, and it means the opposite of turning away.
aver.semantic_hint: What a witness does when they state something positively as fact.

aversion.required_nuance: dislike strong enough to cause avoidance
aversion.mental_hook: Dislike strong enough to make you leave the room.
aversion.semantic_hint: The strong distaste that makes you avoid something entirely.

avert.required_nuance: turning away, or preventing by turning away
avert.mental_hook: Eyes are averted. So are disasters.
avert.semantic_hint: What quick thinking does to a crisis that was about to happen.

avid.mental_hook: The reader who finishes a book a week.
avid.semantic_hint: The adjective for a reader who gets through a book every week.

incorrect_associations.misconception: confuses it with vocation, which is its opposite

avocation.required_nuance: the pursuit beside the job, never the job
avocation.mental_hook: A vocation pays. This one does not.
avocation.semantic_hint: The serious hobby someone keeps up alongside their real job.

avow.semantic_hint: What you do when you admit a belief openly instead of hiding it.

accepted_concepts: benevolent in the manner of an older relative
avuncular.required_nuance: the warmth of an uncle, without a father's authority
avuncular.mental_hook: An uncle's warmth, with none of a father's authority.
avuncular.semantic_hint: The word for a senior colleague who is warm and tolerant like a favourite uncle.

axiom.required_nuance: taken as true without proof, and reasoning starts there
axiom.mental_hook: Where the proof starts, not where it ends.
axiom.semantic_hint: In geometry, the starting truth that everything else is proved from.

axiomatic.required_nuance: so obvious that proving it is unnecessary
axiomatic.semantic_hint: The adjective for a claim so obvious nobody bothers to prove it.

incorrect_associations.misconception: takes the noun sense for the verb

badger.mental_hook: The animal was set upon, and the verb stuck.
badger.semantic_hint: What a reporter does to a politician who will not answer.

badinage.required_nuance: talk that is playful and light, never serious
badinage.mental_hook: Talk for the pleasure of talking.
badinage.semantic_hint: The light teasing talk between friends who are not discussing anything.

incorrect_associations.misconception: hears 'wail' or 'woeful' and swaps menace for grief

baleful.required_nuance: menace, especially carried in a look
baleful.mental_hook: The look across the room that promises trouble.
baleful.semantic_hint: The word for a stare that plainly promises harm.

balk.required_nuance: stopping short and refusing to go on
balk.mental_hook: The horse that stops dead at the fence.
balk.semantic_hint: What a horse does at a fence it will not jump.

incorrect_associations.misconception: takes the noun sense for the verb

balloon.mental_hook: Costs do it. Rarely good news.
balloon.semantic_hint: What a budget does when the costs run away with it.

banal.mental_hook: Not bad. Just heard a thousand times before.
banal.semantic_hint: The word for a remark so ordinary it adds nothing at all.

banality.required_nuance: the dullness itself, or a remark exhibiting it
banality.mental_hook: The thing said at every funeral and every wedding.
banality.semantic_hint: The kind of stale remark that gets said at every wedding speech.

bandy.mental_hook: Names get bandied about. Rarely carefully.
bandy.semantic_hint: What people do with a rumour when they pass it casually around.
